title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS FLORAL TRIBUTES TO SHRI SOMNATH CHATTERJEE
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Lok Sabha Secretariat LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS FLORAL TRIBUTES TO SHRI SOMNATH CHATTERJEE प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 11:57AM by PIB Delhi Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes to former Lok Sabha Speaker, Shri Somnath Chatterjee in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, on his birth anniversary, today. Members of Parliament, former Members of Parliament and other dignitaries also paid floral tributes to Shri Somnath Chatterjee in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, on this occasion. Secretary-General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh also paid tributes to Shri  Chatterjee. Shri Somnath Chatterjee was born on 25 July 1929 in Tezpur, Assam. A distinguished lawyer by profession, he entered active politics in 1968 and was first elected to the Lok Sabha in 1971. Over the course of an exceptional parliamentary career, he served ten consecutive terms as a Member of Parliament. On 4 June 2004, Shri Chatterjee was unanimously elected as the Speaker of the 14th Lok Sabha, a position he held with great distinction until 31 May 2009. Renowned for his intellect, oratory, and deep commitment to parliamentary values, Shri Chatterjee played a pivotal role in elevating the quality of debates in the House. In recognition of his outstanding contributions to the Indian parliamentary system, he was conferred the Outstanding Parliamentarian Award in 1996. During his tenure as Speaker, he introduced several key initiatives to modernize parliamentary functioning. Notably, he oversaw the launch of Lok Sabha Television (LSTV), a 24-hour parliamentary channel, in July 2006, and inaugurated the high-tech Parliamentary Museum in August 2006. A portrait of Shri Somnath Chatterjee graces the Outer Lobby of the erstwhile Lok Sabha Chamber in Samvidhan Sadan. It was painted by Shri Manish Kumar Rao and unveiled on 10.02.2014 by the then President of India Shri Pranab Mukherjee. लोक सभा के पूर्व अध्यक्ष श्री सोमनाथ चटर्जी की जयंती पर आज संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में भावपूर्ण श्रद्धासुमन अर्पित किए। संसदीय परंपराओं के संरक्षण, स्वस्थ लोकतांत्रिक संवाद और सदन की मर्यादा के प्रति उनकी अटूट प्रतिबद्धता सदैव प्रेरणास्रोत रहेगी। pic.twitter.com/0RncKaEVIa — Om Birla (@ombirlakota) July 25, 2026 *** AM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289278) आगंतुक पटल  : 256 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Marathi , Gujarati , Tamil Lok Sabha Secretariat LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS FLORAL TRIBUTES TO SHRI SOMNATH CHATTERJEE प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PM to Interact with Participants of Viksit Vibrant Village Programme 2026 on 26 July
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Prime Minister's Office PM to Interact with Participants of Viksit Vibrant Village Programme 2026 on 26 July Over 400 youth participants, representing every State and Union Territory, were selected for Viksit Vibrant Village Programme 2026 through a nationwide online quiz competition Viksit Vibrant Village Programme 2026 was organised from 4 June to 30 June, connecting youth with 74 Vibrant Border Villages across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand Programme provided participants with first-hand exposure to the socio-economic landscape, cultural heritage and developmental aspirations of India's frontier regions प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 11:10AM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will interact with participants of the Viksit Vibrant Village Programme  2026 on 26 July 2026 at 4:30 PM via video conferencing. The Viksit Vibrant Village Programme, implemented through MY Bharat, has been conceptualised to realise Prime Minister's vision of treating India's border villages as the first villages of the nation and making them active partners in the journey towards Viksit Bharat. Viksit Vibrant Village Programme 2026 was organised in two phases from 4 June to 30 June 2026, covering 74 vibrant villages across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Over 400 youth participants, representing every State and Union Territory, were selected through a nationwide online quiz competition that witnessed participation from more than three lakh youth. As part of the programme, participants lived with local communities and undertook activities such as Swachhta drives, awareness campaigns on Government schemes, Yuva Sammelans, cultural exchange programmes, tree plantation drives, Mini Model Panchayat simulations, interactions with local artisans and visits to institutions of strategic importance. The programme provided participants with first-hand exposure to the socio-economic landscape, cultural heritage and developmental aspirations of India's frontier regions, while fostering community participation, national integration and a deeper understanding of the strategic importance of border villages. *** MJPS/SS/ST (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289270) आगंतुक पटल  : 627 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Telugu , Malayalam , Marathi , Assamese , Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil Prime Minister's Office PM to Interact with Participants of Viksit Vibrant Village Programme 2026 on 26 July Over 400 youth participants, representing every State and Union Territory, were selected for Viksit Vibrant Village Programme 2026 through a nationwide online quiz competition Viksit Vibrant Village Programme 2026 was organised from 4 June to 30 June, connecting youth with 74 Vibrant Border Villages across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand Programme provided participants with first-hand exposure to the socio-economic landscape, cultural heritage and developmental aspirations of India's frontier regions प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha inaugurates Two-Day Orientation Programme 'Prarambh' for the newly elected/nominated Members of Rajya Sabha
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Rajya Sabha Secretariat Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha inaugurates Two-Day Orientation Programme 'Prarambh' for the newly elected/nominated Members of Rajya Sabha United by one document, which is our Constitution, one vision, that is Nation First (Rashtra Pratham), and one goal, a Viksit Bharat @ 2047, says Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan Every policy you frame, every question you ask, every law you enact and every discussion you participate in has the potential to improve countless lives, states Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan Your intervention can change a policy and transform generations, urges Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 3:17PM by PIB Delhi Hon’ble Chairman Rajya Sabha, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan, inaugurated the two-day Orientation Programme ‘ Prarambh’ for the newly elected/nominated Members of the Rajya Sabha in the biennial elections of 2026 today. The inaugural function was attended by the Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Hon’ble Members of Parliament; Secretary-General of Rajya Sabha, Shri P.C. Mody, and senior officers of the Rajya Sabha Secretariat. The two-day Orientation Programme began with a welcome address by Hon'ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh.  Shri Harivansh emphasized that new Members are entering the Parliament of India during 'Amrit Kaal'; and they can play a significant role in building a 'Viksit Bharat @2047' (Developed India @2047). Shri Harivansh enlightened the new Members that they have the right to hold the Government accountable, offer constructive criticism, guide the Government onto the right path, and provide advice. New Members can seek answers from the Government, raise issues of public interest, and offer counsel on bills. In his inaugural address, extending his heartiest congratulations to the newly-elected Members, the Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan noted that 67 Members have entered the August House for the first time. He appreciated their presence on a weekend despite public commitments in their respective States, stating that their attendance reflects a strong commitment toward discharging parliamentary responsibilities and strengthening democratic institutions. Highlighting the unique character of the Upper House, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan described the Rajya Sabha as the cornerstone of India's federal democracy. He remarked that while the House brings together diverse regional voices, Members come together on the floor to strengthen national unity and integration. He remarked that ‘we are united by one document - the Constitution; one vision - Nation First ( Rashtra Pratham ); and one goal—a Viksit Bharat @ 2047’ . Emphasizing the core philosophy of Parliamentary functioning, the Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan stated that while legislators may agree to disagree, there must be absolute commitment to the people and the Constitution, which serves as the common moral compass. Reiterating his key principle, he stated: “Debates, discussions or even disruptions, it must always lead to a decision.” He cautioned that disruptions failing to lead to a discussion toward a decision do not serve the right purpose. Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasized that Question Hour and Zero Hour provide vital opportunities to individual Members and their sanctity must be protected from disruptions. The Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan stressed the importance of acquiring thorough knowledge of the rules and procedures of the House and highlighted that before submitting a notice under Rule 267, understanding the Rule fully is very important. The Rule 267 should only be invoked in the rarest of rare situations and that too with the consensus of the House. Addressing the responsibilities of public representatives, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan noted that while elections are won by votes, respect is earned through public service. He urged Members to remember that every question asked, every law enacted, every policy framed, and every debate participated in has the potential to transform lives. He stated that the present generation of legislators has been given the historical opportunity to fulfill the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 set by Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, by driving progress and expanding opportunities for youth and rural families. Sharing his personal parliamentary experience, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan underscored the power of legislative interventions. He recalled that during his tenure as a Member of the Lok Sabha and Convenor of the Parliamentary Sub-Committee on Textiles, the committee's hard work led to the recommendation and subsequent creation of the Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) by the Central Government, which modernized the textile industry. He urged Members to dedicate themselves whole-heartedly to their roles, noting that even small suggestions during Zero Hour, Question Hour, or Committee meetings can yield major policy transformations. On parliamentary preparation, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan advised Members to adopt a habit of continuous learning, sharing that he personally reviews the day's business and associated procedural rules before every sitting of the House. He encouraged Members to master legislative and budgetary processes, Committee systems, conventions, and parliamentary ethics. Appreciating the Secretary-General and Secretariat officials for designing a comprehensive curriculum, Shri C.P. Radhkrishnan noted that the programme incorporates modern digital needs, including a first-of-its-kind hands-on workshop on IT tools. He emphasized that Parliament has entered the era of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and emerging technologies, pointing out that AI-driven tools like Vani Setu now provide real-time interpretation in multiple languages inside the Rajya Sabha Chamber. He urged Members to actively adopt Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to remain future-ready. Concluding his address, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan wished all newly-elected Members a fruitful Orientation Programme and an enriching legislative journey in the service of the nation. ******* RKK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289341) आगंतुक पटल  : 44 Rajya Sabha Secretariat Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha inaugurates Two-Day Orientation Programme 'Prarambh' for the newly elected/nominated Members of Rajya Sabha United by one document, which is our Constitution, one vision, that is Nation First (Rashtra Pratham), and one goal, a Viksit Bharat @ 2047, says Shri C.P. title: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Urges Centre to Issue Commemorative Coin and Postage Stamp to Mark 150th Prakat Din of Sant Gajanan Maharaj
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau AYUSH Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Urges Centre to Issue Commemorative Coin and Postage Stamp to Mark 150th Prakat Din of Sant Gajanan Maharaj Shri Jadhav Writes to Finance, Communications and Culture Ministers Seeking National Recognition of Sant Gajanan Maharaj's Legacy प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 11:54AM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, has urged the Government of India to commemorate the 150th Prakat Din of the revered saint Shri Sant Gajanan Maharaj by issuing a ₹150 commemorative coin and a commemorative postage stamp. In letters addressed to Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. The Minister expressed confidence that the proposal would receive favourable consideration and provide fitting national recognition to the enduring spiritual and cultural legacy of Shri Sant Gajanan Maharaj. title: Final US Section 301 Measures on Forced Labour: India Placed in Lower Tariff Tier at 10%
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry Final US Section 301 Measures on Forced Labour: India Placed in Lower Tariff Tier at 10% प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 3:36PM by PIB Delhi The United States Trade Representative (USTR) announced on 23rd July 2026 the final measures under Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act, 1974. The measures follow USTR’s investigation into the acts, policies and practices of 60 economies, including India, relating to the imposition and enforcement of prohibitions on the importation of goods produced with forced labour. USTR has imposed an additional 10% ad valorem duty on imports from India. This is a reduction from the 12.5% duty initially proposed on 2nd June 2026.  The Government of India remained closely engaged with USTR throughout the investigation through detailed written submissions and in-person consultations, including participation in public hearings. As a result of these sustained efforts, India has been placed in the lower tier of additional tariffs under the final measures, providing a relative advantage to Indian exports in key sectors. A substantial share of India’s exports to the United States, which currently attract zero additional duties, such as generic pharmaceuticals, smartphones and certain other specified products, continue to remain outside the scope of the additional 10% duty. Further, products already covered under Section 232 measures, including steel, aluminium and auto parts, are not subject to the additional 10% duty. Section 232 duties are applicable broadly to all countries with limited exceptions. On account of these exemptions, an estimated 45% of India’s exports to the United States remain outside the purview of the additional 10% Section 301 duty. The remaining 55% of exports will attract the additional 10% duty, where India’s tariff incidence is comparatively lower than that for most other economies covered by the investigation. The textile specific mechanism referenced in the final measures is yet to be established and operationalised. India continues to engage with the U.S. on this matter as part of the ongoing negotiations for the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement. The Government remains committed to working with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement, as announced on 2nd February 2026 and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026. *** Abhishek Dayal/ Garima Singh/ Ishita Biswas (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289348) आगंतुक पटल  : 49 Ministry of Commerce & Industry Final US Section 301 Measures on Forced Labour: India Placed in Lower Tariff Tier at 10% प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Indian Coast Guard Rescues 170 Persons in Extensive Flood Relief Operations Across Daman, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and South Gujarat
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence Indian Coast Guard Rescues 170 Persons in Extensive Flood Relief Operations Across Daman, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and South Gujarat प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 12:13PM by PIB Delhi Indian Coast Guard, working in close coordination with the civil administration, rescued 170 stranded persons in the flood-hit areas of Daman, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and South Gujarat, through 11 rescue operations conducted since the midnight of 22 July 2026 amidst incessant rainfall, severe flooding and extremely challenging weather conditions. The operations commenced during the night of 22/23 July with the rescue of five stranded persons from Khanvel, Silvassa, followed by the evacuation of three fishermen trapped along the flooded riverbank at the Kadaiya coastal area. In one of the largest rescue missions, 60 persons stranded in the flood-affected Welspun Industrial Area, where road connectivity had been completely disrupted, were safely evacuated during the night of 23/24 July. Subsequent operations included the rescue of seven persons from a bus stranded in floodwaters near Aero Fibre Pvt. Ltd., evacuation of ten persons from Dongri, helicopter rescue of four stranded persons from the Valsad-Pardi area, and overnight evacuation of eight persons from the Reliance Industries area. In another significant rescue mission, the Coast Guard evacuated ten persons from the Avadh Society area, including a nine-month pregnant woman and a woman suffering from respiratory distress, ensuring their timely access to medical care. On 24 July, two Indian Coast Guard helicopters successfully airlifted 33 stranded persons from Mendar Village in Navsari district, including an individual experiencing severe chest pain who was provided urgent medical assistance. Despite relentless rainfall, swift currents and hazardous operating conditions, Coast Guard personnel continued rescue efforts without pause, reaffirming the Service's motto of ‘Vayam Rakshamah’ (We Protect). The Indian Coast Guard remains fully committed to supporting the civil administration and continues to maintain a high state of operational readiness to respond swiftly to any further emergencies arising from the ongoing flood situation. *** SR/PS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289282) आगंतुक पटल  : 286 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil Ministry of Defence Indian Coast Guard Rescues 170 Persons in Extensive Flood Relief Operations Across Daman, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and South Gujarat प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Nandyal District Strengthens Water Conservation Infrastructure and Storage Capacity under Catch the Rain Campaign
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Jal Shakti Nandyal District Strengthens Water Conservation Infrastructure and Storage Capacity under Catch the Rain Campaign प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 2:36PM by PIB Delhi The Catch the Rain Campaign (4th July–4th August 2026) is being implemented across Nandyal District of Andhra Pradesh with the objective of conserving every drop of rainwater through the restoration of traditional water bodies, desilting of feeder channels, revival of tank systems, and creation of additional water storage. The campaign is carried out in convergence with various departments, following the principle of “Catch the Rain, Where it Falls, When it Falls.” Through scientific planning, community participation and coordinated implementation, the district is strengthening its water conservation infrastructure and enhancing its capacity to capture and store monsoon runoff. Scientific Planning and Participatory Implementation : Scientific planning is undertaken across all 489 Gram Panchayats through field surveys, mapping of priority water bodies, feeder channels and watershed areas, and technical assessments by the concerned departments. Consultations with local communities and village elders help identify interventions based on local needs and traditional knowledge. The proposed works are placed before the Gram Sabha to ensure transparency and community participation. Based on this scientific and participatory planning process, the district identifies, sanctions and grounds 2,103 water conservation works, achieving 100% grounding. These interventions are strategically planned to maximise rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and water storage, thereby strengthening the objectives of the Catch the Rain Campaign. Large-Scale Water Conservation Interventions : Under the campaign, 2,691 km of feeder and supply channels are desilted and restored, improving the conveyance of rainwater into tanks and reservoirs. Restoration works are undertaken in 251 Minor Irrigation Tanks, of which 225 works are completed, while the remaining are under progress. The district has also strengthened its network of 22,221 Farm Ponds, 2,221 Check Dams and 202 Percolation Tanks, significantly enhancing rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and water availability across the district. These interventions improve the overall efficiency of the water conservation system and reinforce the district’s preparedness to capture every possible drop of rainfall. Additional Water Storage Capacity Created : The district assesses the additional water storage created through these interventions using technical estimates prepared by the concerned engineering departments. The restoration of feeder channels and water conservation structures is estimated to restore 3.27 TMC of tank storage capacity, while newly created water conservation structures contribute an additional 0.03 TMC of storage. By increasing the capacity of tanks and other water bodies to capture and retain monsoon runoff, these scientifically planned interventions significantly strengthen the Catch the Rain Campaign, improve groundwater recharge, and ensure greater water availability for agriculture, livelihoods and local communities. Towards Sustainable Water Security : The Catch the Rain Campaign continues to strengthen water conservation efforts across Nandyal District through large-scale desilting of 2,691 km of feeder and supply channels, restoration of 251 Minor Irrigation Tanks, implementation of 2,103 water conservation works, and the revival of thousands of rainwater harvesting structures. Driven by scientific planning, technical assessment and active community participation, these interventions enhance the district’s capacity to capture, store and recharge rainwater while improving long-term water security and climate resilience. The district’s integrated approach demonstrates how coordinated action under the Catch the Rain Campaign is creating sustainable water conservation outcomes and advancing the vision of “Catch the Rain, Where it Falls, When it Falls.” *** ND/HM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289321) आगंतुक पटल  : 112 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Tamil Ministry of Jal Shakti Nandyal District Strengthens Water Conservation Infrastructure and Storage Capacity under Catch the Rain Campaign प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Government committed to engaging with employee organisations through regular dialogue and constructive consultations: Dr. Jitendra Singh
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions Government committed to engaging with employee organisations through regular dialogue and constructive consultations: Dr. Jitendra Singh Legacy Service Grievances Pending for Nearly Three Decades Resolved Through Transparent and Employee-Centric Governance: Dr. Jitendra Singh Dr. Jitendra Singh Holds Interaction with Postal Employees' Federation on Service Reforms and Employee Welfare Postal Employees' Federation Appreciates Resolution of Long-Pending Service Issues प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 3:19PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today said that the Government remains committed to engaging with employee organisations through regular dialogue and constructive consultations. The Minister said that the Government's unwavering focus on transparency, accountability and employee welfare has led to the resolution of several legacy service-related grievances that had remained pending for nearly 25 to 30 years. He said responsive governance, timely decision-making and sustained administrative reforms have transformed grievance redressal into a key pillar of public administration, ensuring that long-pending issues of government employees are addressed in a fair, rule-based and time-bound manner. Dr. Jitendra Singh made these observations while interacting with a 12-member delegation of the Bhartiya Postal Employees Federation (BPEF), affiliated with the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS), led by its General Secretary Shri Ananta Kumar Pal, at his official residence in New Delhi. The delegation comprised representatives of postal employees from Bihar, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and several other States, reflecting the Federation's pan-India representation. The delegation discussed a wide range of issues concerning postal employees, including service matters, employee welfare, recognition-related issues and the need for expeditious resolution of pending administrative and legal matters. It also highlighted issues requiring coordinated consideration across departments and sought continued support for addressing genuine employee concerns within the established legal and administrative framework. Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the Government remains committed to engaging with employee organisations through regular dialogue and constructive consultations. He emphasised that every genuine representation is examined on merit and in accordance with the applicable rules and procedures, while matters involving multiple Ministries and Departments require wider institutional consultation to ensure legally sound, transparent and sustainable outcomes. He encouraged employee representatives to continue sharing documented suggestions and feedback to further strengthen governance and public service delivery. The members of the delegation appreciated the Government's sustained emphasis on administrative reforms and acknowledged that several long-pending service-related cases and employee grievances, which had remained unresolved for decades, have received focused attention in recent years. They noted that improvements in grievance redressal mechanisms, transparency and administrative responsiveness have significantly strengthened the confidence of employees in the system. The delegation also appreciated the role of the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) in promoting transparent, accountable and citizen-centric governance through administrative reforms and institutional capacity building. The representatives thanked Dr. Jitendra Singh for maintaining an open and consultative approach with employee organisations and expressed confidence that the Government would continue to address legitimate service-related concerns while further strengthening employee welfare, administrative efficiency and good governance across the country. title: Spudding of first appraisal well, MN-DWN18-1-HD, begins in Mahanadi offshore basin
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas Spudding of first appraisal well, MN-DWN18-1-HD, begins in Mahanadi offshore basin Every metre drilled brings us closer to reducing import dependence, strengthening self-reliance and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat: Sh. Hardeep Singh Puri प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 1:26PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, today marked the commencement of drilling of the first appraisal well, MN-DWN18-1-HD, in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin. Describing the occasion as "the beginning of a new chapter in India's journey towards energy security", the Minister said the commencement of drilling reflects the outcome of a decade of visionary reforms that have transformed India's exploration and production landscape. The MN-DWN18-1-HD appraisal well being spudded today in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin is the first of four planned deepwater wells that will systematically evaluate one of India's most prospective offshore basins. The drilling programme will employ world-class deepwater drilling technology to unlock new hydrocarbon resources and strengthen India's domestic production capability. The Minister said that over the past decade, the Government has fundamentally transformed the exploration and production ecosystem through landmark policy and regulatory reforms. He highlighted the introduction of the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), replacement of the nomination-based approach with the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP), adoption of a transparent Revenue Sharing framework and the opening of nearly 99% of the erstwhile offshore "No-Go" areas for exploration. He noted that nearly 81% of India's active exploration acreage has been awarded after 2014, reflecting the confidence these reforms have inspired among investors and explorers alike. Emphasising the importance of scientific exploration, the Minister said the Government has made sustained investments in geoscientific data generation through initiatives such as Mission Anveshan, the National Seismic Programme, the Extended Continental Shelf Survey, the National Data Repository and the Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study, creating one of the world's most comprehensive geoscientific databases to unlock India's frontier basins. Highlighting the progress achieved under the Government's exploration reforms, Shri Puri said that under OALP, 172 exploration blocks covering nearly 3.8 lakh square kilometres have been awarded with committed investments exceeding USD 4.3 billion. During FY 2025-26 alone, around 674 wells were drilled, five new discoveries were made and seven discoveries were monetised. The Minister said the Government's strategy is two-fold—discovering new hydrocarbon resources while maximising recovery from existing national assets. He added that efforts are also underway to revitalise mature producing fields through the deployment of advanced technologies and global best practices. The Minister emphasised that India's energy future will not be secured by a single discovery but through sustained reforms, cutting-edge technology, scientific exploration and the dedication of thousands of geologists, engineers, scientists and offshore professionals. "As we commence this first well today, we are not merely drilling into the seabed—we are drilling into India's future energy security. Every metre drilled brings us closer to reducing import dependence, strengthening self-reliance and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat," the Minister said. Congratulating ONGC, Oil India Limited, the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons, technical partners and the entire exploration fraternity, Shri Puri expressed confidence that today's commencement of drilling would further strengthen India's offshore exploration efforts and contribute to the country's long-term energy security and goal of energy self-reliance. **** TM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289301) आगंतुक पटल  : 240 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Assamese , Tamil Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas Spudding of first appraisal well, MN-DWN18-1-HD, begins in Mahanadi offshore basin Every metre drilled brings us closer to reducing import dependence, strengthening self-reliance and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat: Sh.                         25 JUL 2026 1:26PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, today marked the commencement of drilling of the first appraisal well, MN-DWN18-1-HD, in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin. Describing the occasion as "the beginning of a new chapter in India's journey towards energy security", the Minister said the commencement of drilling reflects the outcome of a decade of visionary reforms that have transformed India's exploration and production landscape. The MN-DWN18-1-HD appraisal well being spudded today in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin is the first of four planned deepwater wells that will systematically evaluate one of India's most prospective offshore basins. The drilling programme will employ world-class deepwater drilling technology to unlock new hydrocarbon resources and strengthen India's domestic production capability. The Minister said that over the past decade, the Government has fundamentally transformed the exploration and production ecosystem through landmark policy and regulatory reforms. He highlighted the introduction of the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), replacement of the nomination-based approach with the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP), adoption of a transparent Revenue Sharing framework and the opening of nearly 99% of the erstwhile offshore "No-Go" areas for exploration. He noted that nearly 81% of India's active exploration acreage has been awarded after 2014, reflecting the confidence these reforms have inspired among investors and explorers alike. Emphasising the importance of scientific exploration, the Minister said the Government has made sustained investments in geoscientific data generation through initiatives such as Mission Anveshan, the National Seismic Programme, the Extended Continental Shelf Survey, the National Data Repository and the Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study, creating one of the world's most comprehensive geoscientific databases to unlock India's frontier basins. Highlighting the progress achieved under the Government's exploration reforms, Shri Puri said that under OALP, 172 exploration blocks covering nearly 3.8 lakh square kilometres have been awarded with committed investments exceeding USD 4.3 billion. During FY 2025-26 alone, around 674 wells were drilled, five new discoveries were made and seven discoveries were monetised. The Minister said the Government's strategy is two-fold—discovering new hydrocarbon resources while maximising recovery from existing national assets. He added that efforts are also underway to revitalise mature producing fields through the deployment of advanced technologies and global best practices. The Minister emphasised that India's energy future will not be secured by a single discovery but through sustained reforms, cutting-edge technology, scientific exploration and the dedication of thousands of geologists, engineers, scientists and offshore professionals. "As we commence this first well today, we are not merely drilling into the seabed—we are drilling into India's future energy security. Every metre drilled brings us closer to reducing import dependence, strengthening self-reliance and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat," the Minister said. Congratulating ONGC, Oil India Limited, the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons, technical partners and the entire exploration fraternity, Shri Puri expressed confidence that today's commencement of drilling would further strengthen India's offshore exploration efforts and contribute to the country's long-term energy security and goal of energy self-reliance. **** TM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289301)

title: Exhaust of 3,000 Litres of Diesel Replaced with Just Water Vapours: The Story of India's Hydrogen Train
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways Exhaust of 3,000 Litres of Diesel Replaced with Just Water Vapours: The Story of India's Hydrogen Train प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 2:19PM by PIB Delhi The India’s first Hydrogen Train was flagged off between Jind and Sonipat on 17th July, 2026 near Delhi area. So far, the train has travelled over 1200 kilometres seamlessly saving diesel consumption of more than 3200 litres. The Hydrogen Train generates electricity onboard through a chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen. The process produces electricity to power the train while emitting only water vapour as a by-product. There is no smoke, and no tailpipe carbon emissions, making it the cleanest form of rail propulsion currently available. The project is an indigenous effort led by Indian Railways. The 10-coach train has two Hydrogen Driving Power Cars deliver 2,400 kW total power, supported by lithium iron phosphate batteries and hydrogen cylinders. Green hydrogen stored at pressure upto 500 bar, dispensed at 350 bar with a total storage facility of about 3,000 kg, creating Railway's first dedicated hydrogen storage facility at Jind. Multiple independent safety systems detect leaks, heat, flames and smoke, backed by automatic shut-off systems, continuous ventilation, international standards and all mandatory validation. Following the successful operation between Jind and Sonipat, trial on the Delhi route will begin soon. India's Hydrogen Fuel Cell Train is more than a technological achievement. It establishes an indigenous hydrogen rail ecosystem and demonstrates India's commitment to sustainable, zero-emission rail mobility, paving the way for future expansion and global leadership in clean transportation. *** Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289319) आगंतुक पटल  : 187 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Marathi Ministry of Railways Exhaust of 3,000 Litres of Diesel Replaced with Just Water Vapours: The Story of India's Hydrogen Train प्रविष्टि तिथि:
